newsitem.title: USA: Workers sue Crown for race and sex discrimination.
newsitem.headline: Workers sue Crown for race and sex discrimination.

text.p: Refinery workers filed a class-action lawsuit Monday charging Crown Central Petroleum Corp with racial and sexual discrimination, according to court papers.
The class action suit was filed on behalf of more than 200 union and non-union female and African-American employees in U.S. District Court in Beaumont, Texas.

The suit alleges that supervisors at Crown's Pasadena and Tyler, Texas, refineries denied African-American and female workers equal pay and promotions and continually circulated racist and sexually explicit cartoons and handbills.
The workers are seeking declaratory and injunctive relief and monetary damages.
Crown could not be immediately reached for comment.

"The company has cultivated an environment that is openly hostile to African-Americans and female employees. Defendant Crown has maintained a system of discrimination," said the complaint obtained from the federal court.
Crown, which is already being sued on pollution charges, is the fifth U.S. oil firm in the past three years to be hit with a discrimination suit.

Last March, Texaco Inc settled a widely-publicized case filed in 1994 by six black employees for a record $176.1 million. Cases against Shell Oil Pennzoil Co and Coastal Corp are still being negotiated.
The workers at Crown are being represented by Milstein, Hausfeld and Toll, which was involved in the Texaco case, as well as the firm Provost and Humphrey.
